config_name: Legion 5i 15.1 — Core Ultra 7 255HX / RTX 5050 8GB, 16GB DDR5, 1TB SSD, 15.1" WUXGA IPS 165Hz

specs.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5050 Laptop 8GB GDDR7 (full ~115W Legion TGP, MUX)
specs.ports: 2x USB-C (DP, PD), 3x USB-A, HDMI 2.1, RJ45 GbE, 3.5mm

battery.notes: 80 Wh. Inferred from NBC-tested Legion 5 Gen 10 chassis (AMD 9.5h WiFi @150nits); Arrow Lake-HX 255HX more efficient than Raptor-HX. ~1h under load.

offers.name: Lenovo Legion 5i 15.1" 165Hz Gaming Laptop - Intel Core Ultra 7 255HX - 16GB DDR5 - 1TB SSD - RTX 5050 - Windows 11 Home - Eclipse Black

reviews.quote: Lenovo's Legion 5 15 is a very good mainstream gamer, which does not reveal any major issues in our review. The chassis is functional with sufficient ports, a very comfortable keyboard, as well as very good maintenance options.

professional.note: No pro review found for this exact IPS/RTX 5050 config (honest disclosure per SHARED-legion5-ips.md); quoted review is the same Gen 10 chassis with OLED + RTX 5060. Ratings inferred, disclosed.

praises: Cheapest way into the Legion 5 Gen 10 chassis: same full-size cooling, MUX-switch GPU and comfortable 1.6mm-travel numpad keyboard as the $3,600 tiers
IPS panel has zero PWM flicker (NBC lists PWM as a con of the OLED sibling) — the pick for flicker-sensitive users
Anti-glare matte panel handles office and outdoor light far better than the glossy OLED tiers
Best-in-class maintenance for the price: 2x SODIMM to 64GB, 2x M.2 slots, screwed battery, official Lenovo maintenance manual
20-core Arrow Lake-HX CPU is a productivity outlier at this price; Wi-Fi 7 + 5MP webcam with hardware eShutter
complaints: Entry WUXGA IPS panel is the line's weak point — Lenovo spec-sheets list 300-nit/45% NTSC variants for this tier, so colors and brightness are visibly dull vs the 500-nit WQXGA panels
RTX 5050 is the weakest Blackwell part: fine at 1080p/1200p but you'll lean on DLSS in new AAA titles
16GB RAM at checkout — plan an upgrade immediately (2x SODIMM slots make it cheap though)
No card reader; speakers 'could be better' (NBC cons for the chassis)
Fans clearly audible in Performance mode gaming (~44-50 dB(A) measured on the chassis); Legion Gen-10 owner threads report warranty friction and occasional fan-bearing grind on the platform

standouts: Full Legion 5 Gen 10 chassis (MUX GPU, great keyboard, easy upgrades) at the line's lowest price
Flicker-free matte IPS panel — a real readability_dark/readability_bright advantage over the OLED tiers
dealbreakers: Entry-tier display: likely 300-nit/45% NTSC WUXGA panel — the weakest screen in the whole Legion 5 lineup
design_philosophy: Lenovo's mainstream Legion 5 line sells one excellent chassis at many price points; this is the floor of that ladder — full TGP GPU and full maintenance access with the cost cut found in the panel and the smallest Blackwell GPU. It fits buyers who want Legion thermals and upgradability on a budget and will tolerate a basic IPS display.
rating_notes: All ratings inferred from the NBC-reviewed Legion 5 Gen 10 chassis (87%, OLED tiers, SHARED-legion5-oled.md) with IPS panel deltas from SHARED-legion5-ips.md: WUXGA IPS (300-nit/45%NTSC likely per Lenovo spec-sheet variants) -> screen_quality 4.3, readability_bright down, readability_dark up vs OLED (no PWM); RTX 5050 -> gaming 5.0; 255HX Arrow Lake-HX -> battery 7.0 (vs 5.5 for Raptor-HX tiers). Panel variant per-SKU unverified - disclosed. Image URL follows standard BBY CDN pattern, not individually verified.
